description: One conveyance that brought this parcel onto this entity's books: when, from whom, under what authority, and what came with it. Rows are written by convey_parcel and are read-only on the form — the counts record what a migration actually moved, not numbers to retype.

fields.description: Conveyed In is the only thing a surviving record can witness: the parcel it came from was deleted by the same call that wrote this row, so there is nothing left to carry a Conveyed Out. Note is for anything added by hand afterwards.
fields.label: Event Type

fields.description: When the conveyance happened, which is the date on the deed and not the date somebody recorded it here.
fields.label: Effective Date

fields.description: The entity whose books carried this ground before.
fields.label: From Entity

fields.description: The docname this parcel had on the previous entity's books. Deliberately Data rather than Link: that record no longer exists, and a Link to a deleted document is a link Frappe will not let you save.
fields.label: From Docname

fields.description: Why the ground moved and what authorises it — the deed, the assignment, the trust amendment. This is the part of the record nobody can reconstruct later.
fields.label: Reason

fields.description: How many File rows followed the parcel to its new docname.
fields.label: Migrated Attachments

fields.description: How many records pointing at the old parcel were repointed at this one — leases, blocks, irrigation zones, housing units, housing assignments.
fields.label: Relinked Records

fields.description: The same count broken out by register, so a reader can tell 29 housing units from 29 leases.
fields.label: Relink Detail

fields.description: Whether the appraisal report came across. linked means it did; unlinked_needs_reattach means the report is filed under the previous entity and somebody has to re-file it, which is a real piece of work and not a silent loss.
fields.label: Appraisal Document Status

name: Parcel Conveyance Event
